title: The Telemetry Leak
briefing: The Mini Station is a tiny score-keeping game, and its crew are its six code files. Players say their high scores are showing up where they should not. One of the crew is an imposter. Read the evidence REA found in the code, question the crew, catch the one whose story does not match, then call the vote.
plainBriefing: Mini Station is a small number game. Players noticed that their details are ending up somewhere they should not. The app is made of six small parts, and in this game each part is a crew member. One of them is lying about what it really does. Talk to them, look at what the scanner found, and catch the liar.
hints: Not everyone is honest. Compare what each crew member SAYS with what the scanner FOUND. Start with the ones whose story is a promise ("never", "nothing", "only").
Look for the crew member who says it only counts or stores things inside the game, then check whether the scanner found it reaching outside or looking up who you are.
It is Telemetry. Ask it the first and third question, then show the clue about your details and the clue about the internet.
realLife: Plenty of real apps count how you use them. That is fine until they also send who you are. Checking what a program connects to and what it looks up about you is exactly how security people spot it.

q1.text: I just count how often the game is played. Nothing about you, I promise.

q2.text: I do not touch any files.

q3.text: Never leave the ship. I only count, I do not send anything.

verdict: Telemetry swore it only counted plays and never left the ship. The code says otherwise.

why.network: A game that only keeps a high score has no reason to open a connection to an outside server.
why.user-info: Counting plays does not need the player's user name or machine name.
